answer: Clone wallets fail a public quartz frequency board. A newcomer etches a 14-line sonnet plan, hashes it to a fresh key, and locks 1.38 POA for eight epochs. The board names five irregular live pings whose gaps (17, 41, 9, 33, 22 minutes after a chime) are cut from that hash; each ping carries a one-time nonce and a work receipt. Three unclustered raters replay the gaps on the tip. A skipped ping costs 0.055 POA. If two plans share a gap series, or five etches arrive from one wallet in 70 minutes — the cheap fable of a farm — every linked bond is cut 48% and that row stays dark for three epochs.
